output:
Dear Larkspur Lofts Residents,

I am writing about the drone I flew from the roof deck on Saturday, October 31, around 4 p.m., and the concerns it raised. I live in unit 5A and have been a resident here for three years. I want to explain what I was doing, apologize for causing worry, and suggest a way forward.

I am a wedding photographer and was testing a new Halvard Mini 4 drone before photographing a vineyard wedding in Dundee. The flight lasted approximately 11 minutes. Throughout the flight, the camera was pointed west toward the river and the Fremont Bridge, not toward anyone’s windows. I was not filming residents or trying to observe anyone’s private space.

That said, I understand that a drone buzzing or hovering over the courtyard could be unsettling without any explanation. I should have considered how it would look and sound to neighbors before launching it. I am sorry that my flight caused concern.

Anyone who would like to see the full, unedited footage is welcome to knock on my door at 5A or email me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example. I am happy to show it and answer questions.

I also want to address the lobby note. Posting my unit number alongside an accusation of spying and calling me a “creep” was hurtful and inappropriate. Concerns about privacy deserve to be taken seriously, but I ask that we discuss them without personal insults or public accusations.

Our current HOA rules do not address drones. I will ask the board to add the subject to the November 19 meeting agenda, at 7 p.m. in the community room. I will not fly from the roof again until the board decides on a rule.

If something I do causes concern in the future, please speak with me directly or send me an email rather than posting a note. I want everyone here to feel comfortable at home, and I am willing to listen.

Sincerely,  
Jess Okafor  
Unit 5A
